answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed
answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: the IPE (Identificador Provisorio Escolar) system let foreign children without a RUN enrol whatever their status. Mineduc data reported by La Tercera/IdeaPaís show 267,339 foreign pupils in 2023 (7.4% of enrolment), with growth concentrated in basic education. 2024–2025: foreign enrolment kept rising (about 276,000 in 2024), and ChileAtiende still describes IPE as giving children access to admission, enrolment, textbooks, meals and school insurance while they regularise. Known gaps continue in both periods: UNICEF (2022) found IPE does not unlock all benefits (SEP, JUNAEB) and that some northern comunas lack school places; the Defensoría de la Niñez (March 2024) reported more than 3,000 children without a public-school place nationwide, a figure not broken down by migrant status. No documented shift between the two dates, so the starting rating is carried forward.

It tags art. 17 fechaVersion="2021-04-20", which means the original wording stayed in force on 1 January 2023 and on 1 January 2026; later amendments (Ley 21.655 of 2024 and others) did not touch it. The practice evidence is mostly press reports of Mineduc data and NHRI/UNICEF statements, not audits.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The protection answer holds. Art. 17: "El Estado garantizará el acceso a la enseñanza preescolar, básica y media a los extranjeros menores de edad establecidos en Chile, en las mismas condiciones que los nacionales. Tal derecho no podrá denegarse ni limitarse a causa de su condición migratoria irregular..." The 'Effectively Always' rating looks generous. There are documented gaps: IPE holders cannot reach SEP/JUNAEB benefits that depend on the Registro Social de Hogares (UNICEF 2022), and there are shortages of school places in northern regions. 'Usually; Effectively Always' would fit the evidence better.
answers.notes: Protection rests on statute (Ley 21.325 art. 17), not on case law. A bill amending Ley 21.325 that would give nationals priority over irregular migrants in health and education passed the Cámara and was in its second constitutional stage in March 2026 (La Tercera, 25 Mar 2026). It was not law on either date. In the June 2026 consolidated text art. 17 still carries its 2021 version date. Ley 21.430 (2022, children's rights guarantees) adds non-discrimination by migratory status but predates the window.

answers.answer_2023: Yes, but only for certain visa types and migrant statuses (e.g., economic, family, humanitarian, temporary or regular migrants)
answers.answer_2026: Yes, but only for certain visa types and migrant statuses (e.g., economic, family, humanitarian, temporary or regular migrants)
answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed
answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: the CNED data reported by La Tercera show 27,854 foreign students in higher education in 2023; IdeaPaís/Mineduc data show substantial foreign enrolment in adult school education. 2024: foreign higher-education enrolment rose 19.2% to 33,203 (CNED, via La Tercera, Sept 2024). This points to continued access for regular migrants, and I found no documented pattern of exclusion for that group. During 2026 Mineduc stopped issuing the IPE to adults (ChileAtiende: "Desde el 2026 ya no se entregará IPE a personas adultas"). Adults without a RUN therefore need to enrol with the Registro Civil under art. 44 first. This mainly affects irregular adults, whom the starting answer does not cover, and I could not date it to on or before 1 January 2026. No shift is rated.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The citation says 'permanent residents', which is too narrow. Art. 17 inciso 3 of Ley 21.325 says "Los extranjeros podrán acceder a las instituciones de educación superior en igualdad de condiciones que los nacionales", with no status limit on access. The status condition applies only to free tuition (gratuidad). Under art. 103(a) of Ley 21.091 that covers "chileno, extranjero con permanencia definitiva, o extranjero con residencia", the latter only if they completed secondary school in Chile. The 'certain statuses' option still fits, because the free-tuition benefit is conditioned on residence status. The citation should name temporary residents with Chilean secondary schooling as well as permanent residents.
answers.notes: Protection rests on statute, not on case law. I found no ruling in the window that changes the rule. The 2026 change to IPE for adults is an administrative practice described by ChileAtiende without a dated instrument, so I did not record it as an event. A reviewer may want to check whether it took effect before 1 January 2026 and whether it affects adult basic and secondary education (EPJA) for irregular migrants.
